children: The benchmark European wholesale gas price rose above €80 for the first time since the start of 2023 on Wednesday afternoon as the Middle East conflict intensified and ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz escalated.
The Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) was up €3.34 at €79.28 per megawatt hour (MWh) by 1524 GMT, ICE data showed, having earlier touched €80.98.
The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) was 9.00 pence higher at 197.82 pence per therm, having touched 201.12 pence/therm earlier, its highest since December 2022.
Brent crude oil futures also breached $100 a barrel on Wednesday for the first time since late July.
An escalation in fighting by U.S. and Iranian forces deepened concerns over oil and gas supply from the region and how long the conflict will drag on.

Iran said on Wednesday it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers, in the biggest declared wave of tit-for-tat attacks on shipping by both sides since the start of the six-month-old war.
Europe's gas stores are 67.12% full, compared to 79.48% a year ago, latest data from Gas Infrastructure Europe showed.

HSBC forecasts European inventories will reach 73% by Nov. 1, the lowest since data collection began in 2009, and does not expect Qatari LNG exports, excluding damaged capacity, to return to normal until at least early next year.

"The market is now pricing in the tightness. Low storage, sluggish injections, constrained Gulf exports, robust gas-fired power demand and renewed US-Iran escalation weakened confidence in a near-term normalisation of LNG flows," said Sandan Ali, global oil and gas analyst at HSBC.
"TTF has also moved back to a premium to JKM (the Asian benchmark), indicating that Europe is bidding more aggressively for marginal LNG," he added in a research note.

Germany, which has one of the lowest gas storage fills in Europe, has said no government intervention is needed to raise gas storage levels, after a lobby group warned of shortages if the coming winter is very cold.

"It looks increasingly like 2021, when several factors contributed to the increase in gas prices over the year," said Anne-Sophie Corbeau, a research scholar at Columbia University's Center on Global Energy Policy.

Meanwhile, Russia's Kremlin said Europe was paying the price for shunning Russian pipeline gas in the wake of the outbreak of the Russia-Ukraine war by buying on the spot market rather than cheaper Russian options.
